what.text: Refugees and asylum seekers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo live in host countries including Uganda, Burundi, Zambia, Rwanda, and Kenya.
By the end of 2025, there were 1176489 refugees from Democratic Republic of the Congo in all host countries combined.
In that same year, 644537 refugees from Democratic Republic of the Congo were living in Uganda.

why.text: The Armed conflict over the government of DR Congo was active from 2005 to 2008 involving RNL and CNDP, from 2011 to 2014 involving CNPSC, M23, UPCP, APCLS, and Forces of Paul Joseph Mukungubila, and from 2016 to 2025 involving Kamuina Nsapu, RNL, CNPSC, M23, MNR, CMC, UPLC, APCLS, FABB, Mayi Mayi Kyandenga, AFC, and CRP.
The Armed conflict with the Islamic State group, DR Congo was active from 2017 to 2025 involving IS, while recorded disaster hazards in the country included Flood and Storm.

Additional active periods included the Armed conflict over Kongo Kingdom territory, DR Congo involving BDK in 2007 to 2008, 2017, and 2020, and the Armed conflict over Katanga territory, DR Congo involving Kata Katanga in 2013 to 2014 and 2020.

when.text: People living in internal displacement inside Democratic Republic of the Congo because of conflict and violence stood at 1900000 at the end of 2009.
This count reached 6737292 by the end of 2023, during years when the Armed conflict over the government of DR Congo and the Armed conflict with the Islamic State group, DR Congo were active.
The main displacement years took place in 2017 and from 2019 to 2025.

how.text: The sources do not state the displacement routes taken or the specific living conditions of displaced populations.

UNHCR counts people displaced inside Democratic Republic of the Congo by conflict whom UNHCR protects or assists at year end, while IDMC estimates people living in internal displacement inside the country because of conflict and violence at year end.
IDMC also tracks new internal displacements from conflict and disasters as yearly counts of movements rather than individual people.
